messages:
shiva: Running FP8 KV on llama2-13b-reservoir in dedicated pool w/ p4d. Memory looks great (–32%) but p99 latency jumped ~35%. Anyone seen this pattern?

maria: Oof. Did you quantize weights only or KV too?

shiva: Both. FP8 for weights and KV. baseline (fp16 KV, int8 weights) p99=420ms, fp8-kv p99=565ms. p50 roughly same (140ms -> 150ms).

kevin: That smell like dequant hotspot when reading KV. FP8 -> fp16 expand on hot path might not be fused. Do you have perf traces?

shiva: Attached quick logs below from local microbench (single request, 128 ctx):
```
CONFIG: model=llama2-13b, batch=1, seq=128
baseline: mem=78GB, p50=142ms, p95=310ms, p99=420ms
fp8-kv: mem=53GB, p50=150ms, p95=420ms, p99=565ms
cpu% while serving (fp8-kv): 48% (was 26%)
```

anna: Interesting CPU jump. Which kernel backend are you on? cudnn? cutlass?

shiva: cutlass 2.1 + our fused-attn. Looks like KV load path calls `dequant_fp8_to_fp16()` per chunk. It's not vectorized and serialized across heads.

eval-bot: automated run 1775013000: fp8-kv sweep on llama2-13b: accuracy delta (MMLU eval) -0.4% vs baseline; embeddings cos sim change < 0.003.

maria: Accuracy hit is small but perf regression is problem. Two quick options: 1) keep FP8 weights but keep KV in fp16; 2) optimize dequant kernel (fuse into KV gather) or use per-tile fused dequant.

kevin: Agree. Also try INT8 KV (symmetric quant) as a comparison — less exotic but sometimes has faster dequant path because we already have fused int8->fp16 kernels. Can you run INT8-KV microbench?

shiva: Kicked off INT8-kv run (same infra). Preliminary: mem=62GB, p50=148ms, p95=330ms, p99=435ms. So INT8 KV reduces mem less than FP8 but latency much closer to baseline.

anna: That aligns — INT8 path uses our existing u8->fp16 vectorized kernel. FP8 is almost always cheaper memory but requires new decode logic that isn't fused yet.

shiva: Repro steps I used:
```
# quant config used
quant: {
  weights: fp8,\n  kv: fp8,\n  backend: cutlass-fused-attn-v2
  kv_chunk_size: 64
}
run: ./bench --model ll2-13b --seq 128 --batch 1 --mode serve
```

kevin: Can you capture nvprof / Nsight timeline for fp8-kv run and tag the kernel where dequant happens? If it's host-side memcpy+cpu dequant we can hotspot quickly.

shiva: Will run and attach. Also noticed tail latency worse when bursty traffic (simulated 5 concurrent). p99 climbs to 800ms for fp8-kv, INT8 stays ~470ms.

maria: For deployments: maybe default to fp16-KV + FP8 weights for now and mark FP8-KV experimental. We should add a rollout flag in config to gate by pool type and instance family.

infra-bot: FYI: Dedicated pool p4d-24x was using driver 535.86. Update available 536.12 (contains cutlass fixes). Might affect FP8 kernels.

kevin: Good catch. Try 536.12 with FP8-KV — driver+cutlass might include fused paths. If that doesn't fix, opt to implement fused dequant+gather in runtime.

shiva: Logged task INF-ml-212 to prototype fused dequant kernel (owner: kevin). Also adding experiment notes to model card.

anna: Quick checklist for next runs:
- nsight timeline for fp8-kv vs int8-kv
- repeat on cuda driver 536.12
- run with kv_chunk_size 128 and 32 (see effect on memcpy pattern)
- microprofile host vs device time for dequant step

shiva: Thanks. I'll run those today. If driver+cutlass fixes p99, we can consider slow rollout. If not, default to keep KV fp16 and weights fp8.

maria: Also add a short eval to ensure quantized KV doesn't regress hallucination checks for our prompt sets (esp. retrieval augmented prompts). Small accuracy delta hides downstream failure modes.

eval-bot: scheduled: hallucination-smoke (ll2-13b, fp8-kv) -> run queued at 1775014000.

kevin: One more note — AWQ/GPTQ variants we tried previously don't support quantized KV in current toolchain; that path would need separate tooling. Good to document for model onboarding.

shiva: Agree. I'll update the onboarding doc and add a table with mem/latency tradeoffs for FP16-KV, INT8-KV, FP8-KV. Will post results when nvprof data is in. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks — this thread is super helpful. If you want a quick pair on the Nsight capture ping me.

shiva: Will do.
